
```{r}
players <- read.csv("C:/Users/hanke/Projects/Big_Data_Bowl_27/data/players.csv")
game_tracking_2023 <- read.csv("C:/Users/hanke/Projects/Big_Data_Bowl_27/data/game_tracking_2023.csv")
```

# Player Information and Cleaning

First we want to see how often Will Anderson is lining up at a specific position

```{r}
anderson_position = player_play %>%
  filter(nfl_id == 55867)

anderson_position %>%
  count(lined_up_position, sort = TRUE)
```

Will Anderson clearly gets the bulk of his snaps in his rookie year at the EDGE position, meaning he is lined up on the defensive line on the outside, likely attacking the backfield through the B or C gap and attacking the tackle.

Next we are collecting all of the playing information on Will Anderson, as we are focused on seeing how he moves during a play

```{r}
will_anderson <- game_tracking_2023 %>%
  filter(nfl_id == 55867)
```

For this document our focus is going to be on Anderson's first snap of the Texans at Bengals game on November 12, 2023. This play is labeled play_55. Here we are also adding descriptors to our data set to help with understanding the motion of the players.

```{r}
play_55 <- will_anderson %>%
  filter(
    game_id == 2023111202,
    play_id == 55
  ) %>%
  arrange(time)

play_55 <- play_55 %>%
  mutate(body_orientation = case_when(
    o >= 0   & o <= 36  ~ "Left",
    o > 36   & o <= 72  ~ "Forward Left",
    o > 72   & o <= 108 ~ "Forward",
    o > 108  & o <= 144 ~ "Forward Right",
    o > 144  & o <= 180 ~ "Right",
    o > 180  & o <= 216 ~ "Left",
    o > 216  & o <= 252 ~ "Forward Left",
    o > 252  & o <= 288 ~ "Forward",
    o > 288  & o <= 324 ~ "Forward Right",
    o > 324  & o <= 360 ~ "Right",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_ 
  )) %>%
  mutate(direction = case_when(
    dir >= 0   & dir <= 36  ~ "Left",
    dir > 36   & dir <= 72  ~ "Forward Left",
    dir > 72   & dir <= 108 ~ "Forward",
    dir > 108  & dir <= 144 ~ "Forward Right",
    dir > 144  & dir <= 180 ~ "Right",
    dir > 180  & dir <= 216 ~ "Left",
    dir > 216  & dir <= 252 ~ "Forward Left",
    dir > 252  & dir <= 288 ~ "Forward",
    dir > 288  & dir <= 324 ~ "Forward Right",
    dir > 324  & dir <= 360 ~ "Right",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_ 
  ))
```

Now that we have our data set we can make some graphs

## Entire Field Graph

```{r}
ggplot(play_55, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_path(color = "blue", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(color = "red", size = 2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 23.61, color = "black", 
             linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.5, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 29.69, color = "black", 
             linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.5, alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 120), 
                     breaks = seq(0,120, by = 10),
                     expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 53.3), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  coord_fixed() +
  labs(
    title = "Will Anderson's Movement - Play 55 Nov 12",
    x = "Field Length (yards)",
    y = "Field Width (yards)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Close-Up Graph

```{r}
ggplot(play_55, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 23.61,
    color = "black",
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 29.69,
    color = "black",
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_path(color = "blue", linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(color = "red", size = 1.5) +
  coord_cartesian(
    xlim = range(play_55$x, na.rm = TRUE) + c(-1, 1),
    ylim = range(c(play_55$y, 20.5, 32.7), na.rm = TRUE) +
      c(-1, 1)
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 6)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 6)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Will Anderson's Movement - Play 55",
    x = "Yardlines",
    y = "Width"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
